                    ### Question
                    A 35-year-old woman from San Francisco has been refusing to vaccinate her children due to the claims that vaccinations may cause autism in children. Her 10-year-old male child began developing a low-grade fever with a rash that started on his face; as the rash began to spread to his limbs, it slowly disappeared from his face. When the child was taken to a clinic, the physician noticed swollen lymph nodes behind the ears of the child. Which of the following are characteristics of the virus causing these symptoms?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Enveloped, DS linear DNA
opb. Nonenveloped, SS linear DNA
opc. Enveloped, SS + nonsegmented RNA
opd. Enveloped, SS - nonsegmented RNA
ope. Nonenveloped, DS segmented RNA

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The clinical presentation of the 10-year-old male child, including low-grade fever, rash starting on the face and spreading to limbs, and swollen lymph nodes behind the ears, is consistent with rubella virus infection. Rubella is known to cause a characteristic exanthema (rash) and lymphadenopathy, particularly posterior auricular lymphadenopathy. The consensus in virology indicates that rubella virus is an enveloped, single-stranded, nonsegmented RNA virus. Therefore, the correct characteristics of the virus causing these symptoms are 'Enveloped, SS - nonsegmented RNA.' This aligns with the reasoning chains that identified rubella as the likely cause based on the symptoms presented.
